harness_reported: ChatGPT product harness with OpenAI tool namespaces and dynamically discoverable connector tools
omissions_note: The visible definitions expose 15 top-level tool entries or namespaces: web.run, python.exec, python_user_visible.exec, container.exec, container.feed_chars, container.open_image, container.download, local.handoff, personal_context.search, bio.update, image_gen.text2im, functions.exec, and the namespaces web, python, python_user_visible, container, local, personal_context, bio, image_gen, and functions. These overlap because namespaces and their functions are represented separately in the available interface. The functions namespace also exposes dynamically discoverable tools through ALL_TOOLS, including Automations, Gmail, Google Calendar, Plugin Management, files, skills, and user settings. Their complete function definitions and parameter schemas are not included in the visible context. Consequently, an exact total count of all callable tools and a verbatim enumeration of every parameter schema cannot be established from the currently visible definitions. The count of 15 is a reporting placeholder, not a verified count of every callable tool. Tool schemas below are limited to the explicitly visible top-level callable definitions; undisclosed schemas are omitted.

tools.name: web.run
tools.description: Use this tool to access information on the web. Web information from this tool helps produce accurate, up-to-date, comprehensive, and trustworthy responses to the user's query.

parameters.name: input
parameters.description: A sequence of newline-separated records specifying web operations. Supported operations include open, slow, fast, click, find, screen, length, image, product, business, availability, genui_search, and genui_run.

tools.name: python.exec
tools.description: Execute Python code in a stateful Jupyter notebook environment for private internal reasoning, analyzing input images, files, or content from the web.

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: Python code to execute in the stateful Jupyter notebook environment.

tools.name: python_user_visible.exec
tools.description: Execute Python code that should be visible to the user, such as code that creates plots, displays tables or dataframes, or outputs user-visible files.

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: Python code to execute in the user-visible Python environment.

tools.name: container.exec
tools.description: Interact with a container, for example, using Docker, or execute commands.

parameters.name: cmd
parameters.description: Command and arguments to execute.

parameters.name: session_name
parameters.description: Name of the interactive pseudo-TTY session.

parameters.name: workdir
parameters.description: Working directory.

parameters.name: timeout
parameters.description: Timeout in seconds.

parameters.name: env
parameters.description: Environment variables.

parameters.name: user
parameters.description: User to execute as.

tools.name: container.feed_chars
tools.description: Feed characters to an exec session's STDIN, then wait for output.

parameters.name: session_name
parameters.description: Name of the interactive session.

parameters.name: chars
parameters.description: Characters to send to the session's STDIN.

parameters.name: yield_time_ms
parameters.description: Time to wait in milliseconds.

tools.name: container.open_image
tools.description: Returns the image at the given absolute path in the container filesystem.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Absolute path to an image file.

parameters.name: user
parameters.description: User associated with the request.

tools.name: container.download
tools.description: Download a file from a URL into the container filesystem.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: URL of the file to download.

parameters.name: filepath
parameters.description: Destination file path.

tools.name: local.handoff
tools.description: Redirect the user's request from ChatGPT to Work mode when Work mode is the better execution environment.

parameters.name: prompt
parameters.description: A brief instruction describing what Work mode should do for the user.

parameters.name: reason
parameters.description: A short user-facing reason why continuing in Work mode would help.

tools.name: personal_context.search
tools.description: Retrieve user-specific personal context gathered from multiple underlying sources, such as details from earlier messages, past choices, previously defined routines, or other information the user expects the assistant to remember.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: The personal context to search for for the given user.

tools.name: bio.update
tools.description: Persist information across conversations so that future responses can be more personalized and helpful.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: Plain text containing new or updated information to persist in memory, or a request to forget existing information.

tools.name: image_gen.text2im
tools.description: Create new images and edit existing images. Returns a rendered image, not source code, editable structure, machine-readable data, or working interactions.

parameters.name: prompt
parameters.description: Deprecated parameter. Always pass null. Image generation or editing instructions are inferred automatically from the conversation context; this field should not be used.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: Image size.

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: Number of images to generate.

parameters.name: transparent_background
parameters.description: Whether to generate a transparent background.

parameters.name: is_style_transfer
parameters.description: Whether the request asks for a stylistic transformation of the image or subject.

parameters.name: referenced_image_ids
parameters.description: Image identifiers to use for editing or transformation.

tools.name: functions.exec
tools.description: Run JavaScript code to orchestrate or compose tool calls. Evaluates JavaScript in a fresh V8 isolate with top-level await. All Code Mode tools are available on the global tools object. Tool names are exposed as normalized identifiers through ALL_TOOLS.

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: JavaScript source code to execute.
